column1: # *** MAURICIO LERENA AND CASIMIRA MONTANO - THE GENERATION ABOVE THE TRINIDAD NEST. ***
# Found 17 September 2026 by doing what work-list row 137 said to do: searching the free FamilySearch
# collections BY PARENT rather than chasing people by name through a paywalled index.
# *** THE ARCHIVE HAD SIX TRINIDAD FATHERS AND NO GENERATION ABOVE ANY OF THEM. *** It now has one
# couple above one of them, and that couple's children explain three of the four departments the
# current tree pointed at.
child
*** CIPRIANO LERENA MONTANA ***
column2: *** Death registration 1928, FLORES *** - Uruguay Civil Registration Index Card 1900-1937, record 40, entry 1, page 20v. ark 1:1:QG3K-CV5Q
column4: *** THE FINDING. *** `trinidad-flores-kindred.tsv` has a CIPRIANO LERENA who married LAURIANA BELOQUI and baptised Doroteo Donato (1875), Maria Leonor (1877) and Lauriana (1891) at Trinidad. *** This is a Cipriano Lerena dying in the same small department in 1928, with parents named. *** *** GRADED AS AN INDEX, NOT AN ACT: the card says "Image Unavailable", so nothing has been READ. *** And the identification rests on a rare forename in one small department across the right span of years - *** strong, and not airtight, because two Ciprianos are possible. ***

column1: *** CLARA LERENA (de PALLARES) ***
column2: *** Death registration 3 March 1925, MONTEVIDEO, certificate 47 *** , aged 77, estimated birth 1848. Husband REYNALDO PALLARES. ark 1:1:XMMG-TNSK. *** This one HAS an image. ***
column4: *** THIS IS ALMOST CERTAINLY THE TREE'S "DEMETRIA CLARA LERENA MONTANO", b. 22 December 1848, San Jose. *** Forename, birth year and the mother's surname all agree - *** and the record EXPLAINS the tree's compound name, which no tree ever does: she is "Lerena Montano" because her mother was CASIMIRA MONTANO. *** *** ONE DISAGREEMENT, LEFT STANDING: the tree gives her death as 1930 and the register says 3 March 1925. ***

column1: # *** WHAT THIS DOES TO THE "FOUR DEPARTMENTS". ***
# Work-list row 120 took four Uruguayan Lerenas in four departments off the current tree and treated
# them as four leads. *** They are not four leads. Three of the four departments are accounted for by
# the children of ONE COUPLE: *** San Jose de Mayo (Ignacia, 1850), Trinidad in Flores (Cipriano,
# Manuel, Ignacia), and Florida (Mauricio junior, 1878). *** Add Salto and Montevideo and this is a
# single family spreading across the Uruguayan interior in one generation. ***
# *** Only ROSARIO in COLONIA is still unaccounted for. ***
# *** AND WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. ***
# *** It does not touch Pablo Armando. *** Nothing here reaches Argentina, and nothing here names a
# Juan Carlos. *** It does not join the Trinidad nest to SANCHO either *** - Mauricio Lerena's own
# parents are still unknown, and until they are found the nest and the Canelones trunk remain two
# separate documented families that share a surname.
# *** THE NEXT STEP IS EXACTLY ONE MORE RUNG: find MAURICIO LERENA's own marriage or baptism. *** He
# was fathering children by 1838, so he was born about 1810-1818 - *** which is the generation of
# Sancho's own children, and therefore the generation where the two families either meet or do not. ***
